title: Add quantization profile canary scenarios (baseline vs profile-enabled) with thresholds + bisect hints
author: Jonas Weber
body: Summary: This PR adds perf-canary coverage for the Quantization Profile Library route-level enablement by introducing paired scenarios that run baseline (default precision) vs profile-enabled execution for the same model/workload mix, then compares deltas against explicit thresholds. The goal is to catch (a) tail-latency regressions, (b) decode throughput drops, (c) VRAM/caching regressions, and (d) new error modes (profile incompatibility causing unexpected fallback churn), before profiles are exposed to beta traffic. Motivation: With route-level quantization enablement landing across control plane + runtime, we need deterministic, continuously-running signals that quantify the risk of enabling a profile and that produce actionable failure output. These scenarios are intended to run on the same infra as existing decode/tps canaries and to surface “bisect hints” that point engineers to likely layers (policy resolution vs artifact fetch vs kernel path vs cache pressure). What’s included: (1) A new scenario type `quant_profile_compare` that executes two runs (baseline + enabled) using identical prompts and compares p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, and error rate. (2) Scenario templates for two context regimes (short chat-style: 256 in / 256 out; long-context: 4k in / 512 out) to exercise KV cache behavior. (3) GPU matrix support (A100-80GB + H100-80GB) with per-SKU thresholds (H100 has stricter decode latency deltas due to kernel selection differences; A100 has stricter VRAM headroom thresholds). (4) Failure classification + automated bisect hints printed in the canary report, including common patterns: “metadata fetch spike / registry throttling”, “fallback rate elevated due to incompatibility”, “decode-only regression likely kernel path”, “prefill regression likely activation quantization / cache fragmentation”. (5) Wiring to export new comparison metrics so dashboards can slice by route/model/gpu and track trendlines over time. Notes/constraints: The scenarios default to running against a pinned model + pinned quantization_profile_ref in staging/perf-canary environments to avoid accidental drift. The scenario runner enforces determinism flags and pins seed where supported to reduce noise (still non-deterministic at token level; we only gate on perf/infra metrics). Thresholds were chosen based on last 14d baseline variance plus an additional buffer for multi-tenant noise; see `docs/quant_profile_compare.md` in this PR for rationale. Rollout: Add scenarios disabled-by-default behind `ENABLE_QUANT_PROFILE_CANARIES` until the control plane config endpoints are fully deployed in perf-canary. Once available, we’ll enable in staging for 48h, then production canary at low frequency before full schedule. Follow-ups: Add a third workload focused on tool-calling/structured output once the runtime path is fully aligned (out of scope here).
commits: a8c9d4e canary: add quant_profile_compare scenario runner
c1b2f37 canary: add baseline vs profile-enabled comparator + delta gating
9e4aa12 canary: add scenario configs for short + long context regimes
d02b1ee canary: export comparison metrics (quant_profile_enabled, delta_p95_ms, fallback_rate)
7bbff0a docs: add guidance on thresholds + interpreting bisect hints
1f6d0c8 chore: stabilize prompt fixtures + enforce seed pinning where supported
3c7fd21 fix: classify registry fetch timeouts separately from runtime 5xx
conversation: Connor O'Brien (review): Can we ensure these scenarios don’t accidentally run against an unpinned `recommended` alias? We should avoid silent drift in canary outputs. Also, what’s the plan if the control plane endpoint is unavailable in perf-canary? Jonas Weber (author): Good call. I updated the config schema to require an explicit `quantization_profile_ref` (no aliases) for this scenario type, and added a preflight check that skips (not fails) with a clear reason if `route-settings` endpoints return 404/501 in the target environment. Mateo Alvarez (review): The bisect hints are great but please make sure we’re not implying root cause too strongly. Can we phrase them as “likely” and include the key metrics that triggered the hint? Jonas Weber (author): Updated hint strings to “likely” and included the triggering signals in the report output: metadata_fetch_p95, fallback_rate, decode_p95_delta, vram_peak_delta. Hiro Tanaka (review): For decode regressions, it would help to print whether the enabled run actually applied the profile or fell back. Otherwise a large delta might just be fallback churn. Jonas Weber (author): Added `resolution_outcome` to the scenario summary (applied/fallback/disabled) and a per-iteration counter. Aisha Bello (review): Thresholds: please align error-rate gating with SRE standards (treat 429/503 separately from 5xx). Also add a hard cap on new 5xx spikes even if latency is within thresholds. Jonas Weber (author): Done: split error buckets and added `new_5xx_rate <= 0.05%` gate, plus a “registry throttling suspected” hint when 429 spikes coincide with metadata_fetch latency. Connor O'Brien (follow-up): Please add the flag to keep these disabled by default until we confirm prod scheduler capacity. Jonas Weber (author): Added `ENABLE_QUANT_PROFILE_CANARIES=false` default and documented enablement steps in the doc. Connor O'Brien: Approved after last push. Mateo Alvarez: Approved. Aisha Bello: Approved.
checks: CI: lint (pass); unit tests (pass); scenario dry-run (pass); typecheck (pass); docs build (pass). Initial run: scenario dry-run failed once due to missing env var for route settings base URL; fixed in 1f6d0c8 and re-ran successfully.
release_notes: perf-canary: Added quantization profile comparison scenarios (baseline vs profile-enabled) with explicit thresholds and actionable bisect hints. Scenarios are disabled by default behind ENABLE_QUANT_PROFILE_CANARIES.
